tables.title: Your people and the residents of your area, by group

working.title: Loaded the census figures
working.detail: Residents by ethnic group in 3 local authorities in England and Wales. From TS021 - Ethnic group (NM_2041_1). Fetched from Nomis.

working.title: Matched your labels to census groups
working.detail: 6 distinct labels. 1 were set by the 'groups' option and the rest were matched by their wording. 187 people were matched to a group and 11 were not, 2 of them with no label.

working.title: Set your people against residents
working.detail: Catchment: Greenwich, Lewisham. You set the catchment. It had 600,000 residents in the census. For each group, its share of your people was divided by its share of residents. A group is under-represented when the result is below 0.8.

working.title: Hid small counts
working.detail: Counts from 1 to 4 for a group were hidden, along with anything that would let them be worked out. 2 cells were hidden.

choices.label: What people are grouped by
choices.reason: It is what the 'characteristic' option says.

choices.label: Groups compared
choices.reason: These are the groups the 2021 Census publishes for every local authority. Your labels were matched to them by their wording, unless the 'groups' option set them.

choices.label: What counts as under-represented
choices.reason: A share of your people below four fifths of the share of residents is a common first test of a gap.

choices.label: Smallest count shown
choices.reason: Smaller counts could point at individuals, so they are hidden.

checks.question: Does each count stand for people, with nobody counted twice?
checks.why: The counts are added up as they are.

checks.question: Were your labels matched to the right groups: Asian, Black, Mixed, White, Other?
checks.why: Labels were matched by their wording, which can be wrong for codes and short forms. Compare the counts with your own, and set any label with the 'groups' option.

checks.question: Did people describe themselves?
checks.why: The census records what people said about themselves. A group recorded by staff may not match it.

checks.question: Is this the area you serve: Greenwich, Lewisham?
checks.why: Your people are set against everyone who lives in this area. A different area has a different make-up.

checks.question: Does the data cover the period you are reporting on?
checks.why: The lens cannot tell which dates the rows are from.

caveats: A gap is not proof of a barrier. Groups differ in age and in need, so a service for older people, say, will not match all residents.
Residents are everyone counted in the area on census day, 21 March 2021, of every age. The make-up of some areas has changed since.
With few people, a gap between two shares can be chance.
The five groups are broad. A group that looks well reached can hold smaller communities that are not.
warnings: 11 people have no label, or a label that matched no census group. They are left out of the shares. Use the 'groups' option to say which group a label belongs to.

sources.name: TS021 - Ethnic group (NM_2041_1)
sources.publisher: Office for National Statistics, through Nomis
sources.used_for: Residents by ethnic group, for comparison.

notes: A count is hidden when it is small and is about a group.
A hidden count is not always small. When only one count in a table is small, a second is hidden with it, so the first cannot be worked out from the total.
The result names census groups, never the labels in your data.
The number of people matched to no group is shown even when it is small, because it says nothing about which group they are in.
The census figures are public counts and are shown in full.
A second run with a different catchment gives a second set of counts. Publish one, because a small count can be worked out by taking one from the other.
